summary.name: Cybertiks
summary.one_liner: Cybertiks is an Earth observation platform that detects sargassum from satellite data and forecasts which beach it will reach within 72 hours, with the source of each figure shown.
use_cases: tracking sargassum from origin to coastline
forecasting which beach sargassum will reach in 72 hours
backing reports or accountability with dated, traceable data
summary.what_it_does: The platform combines satellite, ocean and atmospheric model, field sensor and operational data into one place. It uses wind and current data in transport models to estimate where sargassum is heading, not only where it was. An agent queries the needed sources, reasons over them and returns a readable reading that cites where each number came from. Each station reports wind, current, wave and resulting drift at 72 hours, and model assumptions such as the wind drag coefficient are visible. The page says it states what cannot be known with the available data rather than filling gaps with estimates.
notable: Public demo running on live data; accounts are opened after a meeting
Every figure shows its source and model, with dated and traceable observations
Drift forecasts cover the Sargasso Sea, the Atlantic belt (GASB) and the Mexican Caribbean coast
Not tied to one satellite or sector; configurable zones, alert cadence and data layers
caveats: Accounts are not self-serve; they are set up after a meeting, so there is no automatic sign-up
Pricing is not stated on the page
The page does not say which satellites or models are used
